decision: Pick B, conditionally, with C as the default until every B control is implemented and offline-tested. A is rejected: even requiring >=2 distinct selected citations, placing remote text in canonical hypotheses conflates provenance, implies canonical graph support and two-source corroboration that the offline graph does not contain, and lets citation formatting masquerade as verification; a citation list alone does NOT make a remote annotation true, canonical, corroborated, or calibrated. B is the safest minimal integration: remote candidates live ONLY in a separate metaAnnotations section, never in hypotheses, never as graph nodes/edges, never altering graph state, HUMAN_REVIEW gate, or caution score, always labeled unverified remote annotation, synthetic-only, not a diagnosis. C is safest in absolute risk and remains the fallback: if separate storage/UI, distinct-citation validation before dedup display, atomic budget reservation, strict parser, or telemetry separation cannot be shipped together, disable enrichment entirely. Staged migration: Stage 0=C/off by default; Stage 1=B behind ENABLED+CREDITS_CONFIRMED+allowed-case+non-conflicting+key-present+reserved budget, stub-tested only; Stage 2=limited fictional demo with kill switch reverting to C; no stage may move metaAnnotations into hypotheses or auto-create edges.

prioritizedFindings.risk: A one-citation remote label displayed beside canonical two-citation hypotheses invents corroboration and contradicts a graph containing only offline nodes/edges; users cannot distinguish deterministic canonical output from uncalibrated remote text.
prioritizedFindings.fix: Separate metaAnnotations type, storage, UI heading, and styling; forbid writes from remote path to hypotheses, graph, safetyGate, or cautionScore.

prioritizedFindings.finding: Distinct-citation validation can be bypassed by duplicates
prioritizedFindings.risk: Validating list length before dedup accepts [e2,e2] or two copies of one annotation/source as if two sources; dedup after validation shrinks support silently.
prioritizedFindings.fix: Normalize, dedup, then require >=2 DISTINCT selected IDs for any annotation shown as multi-source; otherwise reject that annotation entirely, do not repair it.

prioritizedFindings.risk: e1+e4 must force HUMAN_REVIEW and block enrichment; client/model output must never override that state or present an unrelated hypothesis except review_required in canonical flow, and never via remote annotations.
prioritizedFindings.fix: Server recomputes canonical state from selected IDs only; if conflict, no HTTP dispatch and no metaAnnotations display.

prioritizedFindings.finding: Untrusted text injection in both directions
prioritizedFindings.risk: Adversarial fictional observation strings can carry prompt-injection, and remote labels can carry instructions, markup, or Unicode bidi controls that spoof citations/UI order.
prioritizedFindings.fix: Send only allowlisted case ID and selected IDs/canonical server-side texts, treat all remote text as inert data, reject control/bidi/non-printable chars, encode on display, never execute or follow label instructions.

prioritizedFindings.finding: Non-atomic spend/call-limit enforcement and false fallback claims
prioritizedFindings.risk: Check-then-call races or per-process counters can exceed budget across instances/restarts; fallback text claiming a remote call happened when gated/timed out corrupts accounting and trust.
prioritizedFindings.fix: Atomically reserve one call slot before dispatch, release only if never dispatched, count dispatched attempts permanently for the process, and make fallback say no remote annotation was accepted.

prioritizedFindings.risk: Unexpected shape, extra fields, graph-edge payloads, malformed finish_reason, truncation, redirects, oversized bodies, 429/5xx, or timeout can be partially accepted or leak into UI.
prioritizedFindings.fix: Fixed destination only, no redirects, 6s timeout, 32KB streaming cap, 256 output-token request limit, strict schema, allowlist finish_reason values, fail closed with zero partial annotations.

prioritizedFindings.finding: Telemetry conflates attempt, completion, and acceptance
prioritizedFindings.risk: Logging a gate block, HTTP error, parsed response, and accepted annotation as the same event overstates reliability and spend and may record unnecessary content.
prioritizedFindings.fix: Record only enum counters: attemptedCall, completedResponse, acceptedAnnotation, rejectReasonCode, caseIdAllowlisted, selectedIdCount; no keys, no raw prompts/responses, no user data.

prioritizedFindings.risk: Even a valid two-citation remote label may be plausible but wrong; labels/citations are provenance pointers, not truth, calibration, or diagnostic reliability.
prioritizedFindings.fix: UI copy: Remote annotation, unverified, synthetic demonstration only, not a diagnosis; no confidence percentage, no certainty language, no graph edge implied.

rejectedShortcuts: Do not auto-add AI-suggested graph edges: remote text has no canonical rule provenance, edge endpoints may be invented, and a displayed link that disagrees with its actual source/target breaks the teaching contract.
Do not move remote labels into hypotheses after adding citations: citations are pointers to selected fictional observations, not evidence of truth, replication, calibration, or real-world certainty.
Do not lower the bar to one citation for remote text and call it corroborated: one source, or [e2,e2] deduped to one, is single-source by definition.
Do not dedup after validation, accept partial/truncated JSON, follow redirects, retry blindly on 429, or let finish_reason synonyms pass: each creates silent partial trust or spend amplification.

Do not let client or model output override HUMAN_REVIEW, caution score, allowed-case gates, or budget state, and do not claim in fallback/UI/telemetry that a remote call completed or was accepted when it was gated, timed out, rejected, or never dispatched.
Do not present any output as a diagnosis, verified finding, confidence score, or production capability; this is a synthetic educational demonstration only.
residualRisks: Synthetic-only limits remain: fictional IDs e1-e4 and invented labels cannot establish real-world facts, transfer to real vehicles, or support repair/safety decisions, and no such inference should be made.

No calibrated diagnostic reliability exists: even a schema-valid, two-citation remote annotation can be fluent and wrong; the caution score is uncalibrated and must not be reinterpreted as probability.
Per-process call limits are not global budget guarantees across instances, restarts, or deployments; without a stronger server-side budget authority the safe posture is off/C.

Remote availability, latency, model behavior, and pricing can change; fail-closed stubs in tests prove contract handling, not live service behavior, and no paid or production access is proposed or required.
Strict printable-ASCII-style label checks may reject legitimate Unicode teaching text; any broadening needs explicit normalization, bidi/control rejection, and display-encoding tests.
Separate metaAnnotations UI still carries anchoring risk: users may over-weight remote text despite labels, so default-off, prominent unverified wording, and revert-to-C kill switch remain necessary.
